newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JUNE 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JUNE 26.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Although shareholders of IPB bank had hoped that the cabinet would decide who would buy the state's 31.5 percent stake, the cabinet did not discuss the matter yesterday. At a general meeting today, shareholders plan to change regulations which concern entry of a strategic partner, and they should approve dividends.
- According to a cabinet decision yesterday, the cabinet should sign a protcol for entry into NATO this year. The document must also be signed by all NATO countries.
- Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus denied yesterday that energy prices would double by the year 2000, according to the energy policy approved on Tuesday.
- Kaucuk Kralupy will obtain a seven-year syndicated credit of 250 million marks from 14 foreign and two domestic banks, arranged by ABN AMRO bank.
- For coordinating preparations for the Czech Republic's entry into NATO, the cabinet approved the establishment of a Committee for Integrating the Czech Republic to NATO.
- Severoceske Teplarny a.s., a leading manufacturer and distributor of heat and hot water, was taken over by an American investor through its subsidiary Horizon Energy Development s.r.o.
MLADA FRONTA DNES - Parliament took one more step towards decreasing taxes for businesses. The relevent committee recommended yesterday that this tax decrease by six points, to 33 percent.

- President Vaclav Havel said he will announce whether he will be a candidate for the presidency next year at the latest before his vacation this year, which he will spend in the Czech Republic in the second half of July.
- Last week, without informing the public, the cabinet approved a proposal from the Finance Ministry to sell the majority stake in Leciva, 66 percent to the company's management.

- The National Property Fund is currently meeting with the management of Mostecke Unelny about selling 15 percent of the state's stake to the management. The remainder would be sold on the capital market.
- The budgetary committee in parliament yesterday approved the cabinet's plans for budget cuts of nearly 17 billion crowns.

- Heinz-PMV, the dominant domestic manufacturer of baby and children's food, had losses last year of 39 million crowns, which was primarily caused by loss-making sales of powdered milk and butter for export.
- Prazska Energetika's profits for last year of 322.379 million crowns will remain for the most part undivided. A small part will go to strengthen reserves and social funds.

PRAVO - Health Minister Jan Strasky (ODS) wants patients to pay 10 percent of the price of medicines. The cabinet did not approve his proposal for a law on public insurance due to the participation of patients. The second proposal, for health care, was approved.

- British Aerospace and Swedish Saab are offering the Czech Republic supermodern fourth generation Gripen fighter jets and also direct cooperation with domestic companies Aero Vodochody, Letov, LET Kunovice or Omnipol.

- All significant rates on the interbank market declined to below 19 percent. Rates for loans for one week to 12 months are between 18.86 and 15.70 percent, according to Czech National Bank spokesman Martin Svehla.

- During its meeting on Wednesday, the cabinet did not approve the proposal to exchange T-72 tanks for L-39 aircrafts and cannon systems with Algeria and instructed Defence Minister Miloslav Vyborny to rework the material.

LIDOVE NOVINY - The city of Prague will decide today about issuing bonds worth nine billion crowns based on a proposal from Mayor Jan Koukal. The plan is not liked by Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus and the central bank.
- Last year, tourists in the Czech Republic spent more than $150 million through VISA cards, an increase of 50 percent over 1995.
- Czech metal companies affected by the EU's antidumping measures against seamless iron pipes will meet with EU officials in Brussels today.
-- Prague Newsroom, 420-2-2423-0003
